title: Fidelity Guard: prioritized synthetic checks on model pin upgrades
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Objective: Implement a prioritized, resource-aware automated eval trigger system ("Fidelity Guard") that runs targeted synthetic checks when a model version is pinned or a catalog upgrade is applied. The system should cover both catalog-wide promotions and tenant/customer pin actions, produce a lightweight impact score, and integrate with the Console and rollout engine without causing undue cost or capacity contention.

Background: We already run various preflight and canary evals for pins, but current mechanisms are either too heavy (full evals on every pin) or too ad-hoc (manual QA/PR-triggered tests). Teams need a safer, automated gating mechanism that balances coverage and cost, surfaces regressions quickly, and ties directly to rollout policies.

Scope: - Trigger prioritized synthetic evals on: (a) catalog-level model promotions, (b) customer/tenant model pin events. - Support configurable sampling, prioritization tiers (critical customers vs low-impact tenants), and a budget cap per event. - Compute a lightweight impact score and map to Console alerts + rollout decision hints. - Integrate with existing eval runner, canary rollout engine, and event bus. - Expose controls for sampling rates and cost budgets in Console.

Non-goals: - Running full-scale offline eval suites on every pin. - Automatic forced rollback without human-in-the-loop for enterprise customers (we will provide an optional auto-fallback policy but default is notify + guidance).

Success metrics: - 90% of catalog pins and 75% of customer pins trigger at least one synthetic check in production during rollout. - Mean time-to-detect quality regressions <= 30 minutes for prioritized tenants. - Alert noise limited to <10% false positives as measured by downstream triage. - Additional hosting cost < 0.5% of monthly inference spend for most customers.
acceptance_criteria: Automated triggers fire for both catalog promotions and customer pin events and are visible in the event log
Console shows per-pin impact summary with impact score, top failing prompt categories, and cost estimate
Configurable sampling tiers (high/medium/low) respected per-tenant and per-project settings
Eval runner enforces a budget cap and gracefully degrades (sample less / shorter tests) when quota reached
Integration with rollout engine surfaces a canary-health signal and an optional auto-fallback flag
Telemetry (latency, tokens consumed, failures) emitted and available in per-route dashboards
Runbook for actionable alerts and an initial support rotation for triage documented

comments: 2026-02-20 Avery Chen: Initial ticket created after Q1 roadmap sync. Goal is to reduce manual QA and speed detection for pinned upgrades. Asked Eng to scope costs and runtime impact.

2026-02-24 Ravi Patel: Scoping meeting with Runtime and Eval teams. Key trade-off: depth of synthetic checks vs cost. Proposal: two-tier checks — fast smoke (latency + core prompt fidelity) and medium checks (diverse prompt set, safety heuristics).
2026-02-26 Priya Verma (Eng): Suggested budget enforcement at the event level and reuse of existing cached KV prefixes to avoid cold-start noise. Noted ENG-2411 has some reusable activation hooks.

2026-02-28 Design review notes: DES feedback to expose sampling as percentage sliders and to include an 'affected use-cases' breakdown in the summary. Mockups uploaded: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1FidelityGuardMocks

2026-03-01 Ravi Patel: Decided to implement prioritized sampling: (1) SLA customers -> always run fast smoke + one medium check, (2) high-traffic projects -> medium probability, (3) low-impact tenants -> sampled at 5%. Also agreed on a hard token budget per event to cap cost.
2026-03-01 Engineering PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/3489 — adds event listener and budget enforcement. Marking for code review.
2026-03-01 QA note: Need to check KV cache warmup strategy to avoid false regressions from cold cache. Added test case to tasks.
